questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The longest river in India is:
questions.explanation: The Ganga (2,525 km within India) is the longest river flowing entirely/mostly within India. Yamuna (1,376 km) is a tributary of the Ganga. Godavari (1,465 km) is the longest peninsular river. Brahmaputra is longer overall but mostly flows through Tibet and Bangladesh.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Ganga river system:

(i) The Ganga originates from the Gangotri glacier as the Bhagirathi river.
(ii) Yamuna, Son, and Ghaghara are major tributaries of the Ganga.
(iii) The Ganga empties into the Bay of Bengal forming the Sundarbans delta.
(iv) The Ganga flows through only one Indian state.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Ganga starts as Bhagirathi from Gangotri glacier in Uttarakhand. (ii) is correct — all three are major Ganga tributaries. (iii) is correct — the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta (Sundarbans) is the world's largest delta. (iv) is wrong — the Ganga flows through Uttarakhand, UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, and West Bengal (5 states).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Godavari river is often called the 'Dakshin Ganga' because:
options: It is the longest river of peninsular India and holds religious significance similar to the Ganga
It originates from the same glacier as the Ganga
It is a tributary of the Ganga
questions.correctAnswer: It is the longest river of peninsular India and holds religious significance similar to the Ganga
questions.explanation: Godavari is called 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganga of the South) because it is the longest peninsular river (1,465 km) and is revered like the Ganga. It doesn't flow through Delhi. It originates from Trimbakeshwar, Maharashtra (not Gangotri). It is NOT a tributary of the Ganga — it's an independent river system.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Most peninsular rivers flow from west to east and drain into the Bay of Bengal.
Reason (R): The Deccan Plateau has a general slope from west to east, with the Western Ghats being higher than the Eastern Ghats.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Mahanadi all flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal. (R) is correct — the Western Ghats form the water divide and the plateau slopes east. (R) explains (A) because rivers naturally flow downhill, and the westward-higher/eastward-lower tilt causes eastward flow.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following rivers with their origins:

Column I:
(a) Ganga
(b) Yamuna
(c) Narmada
(d) Kaveri

Column II:
(i) Amarkantak (Madhya Pradesh)
(ii) Yamunotri glacier (Uttarakhand)
(iii) Talakaveri (Brahmagiri hills, Karnataka)
(iv) Gangotri glacier (Uttarakhand)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Ganga originates from Gangotri glacier (iv). Yamuna from Yamunotri glacier (ii). Narmada from Amarkantak plateau (i). Kaveri from Talakaveri in Karnataka (iii). Option 2 swaps Ganga and Yamuna. Option 3 swaps Yamuna and Narmada. Option 4 swaps Ganga and Narmada.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following rivers flow WESTWARD and drain into the Arabian Sea?

(i) Narmada
(ii) Tapi (Tapti)
(iii) Krishna
(iv) Mahi

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Narmada (i), Tapi (ii), and Mahi (iv) all flow westward into the Arabian Sea. They are exceptions to the general eastward flow of peninsular rivers. Krishna (iii) flows EASTWARD into the Bay of Bengal, not the Arabian Sea.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Chilika Lake, Asia's largest brackish water lagoon, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Chilika Lake is in Odisha on the east coast. It's Asia's largest brackish water lagoon and a Ramsar wetland site. Kerala has Vembanad Lake. Andhra Pradesh has Kolleru Lake. West Bengal has the Sundarbans wetlands.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Brahmaputra river:

(i) It originates near Mansarovar Lake in Tibet as the Tsangpo.
(ii) It enters India through Arunachal Pradesh where it is called the Dihang.
(iii) It is known for causing devastating floods in Assam.
(iv) It drains into the Arabian Sea.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Brahmaputra rises near Mansarovar as Tsangpo in Tibet. (ii) is correct — enters India in Arunachal Pradesh as Dihang/Siang. (iii) is correct — annual floods in Assam's Brahmaputra valley are severe. (iv) is wrong — it drains into the Bay of Bengal (through Bangladesh as the Jamuna/Padma), NOT the Arabian Sea.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Narmada and Tapi rivers flow through rift valleys.
Reason (R): Unlike most peninsular rivers that flow in shallow valleys eroded over time, the Narmada and Tapi flow in deep, narrow, fault-formed trenches between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — both rivers occupy rift/fault valleys. (R) is correct — they flow in linear depressions formed by geological faulting between mountain ranges. (R) explains (A) by describing the geological formation (faulting between Vindhya and Satpura) that created the rift valleys.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Wular Lake, the largest freshwater lake in India, is located in:
questions.explanation: Wular Lake is in the Bandipora district of J&K — it's India's largest freshwater lake. Rajasthan has Sambhar (salt) Lake. Uttarakhand has smaller lakes like Nainital. Himachal has Dal Lake (Kangra) and Renuka Lake.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following rivers with the seas/bays they drain into:

Column I:
(a) Ganga
(b) Narmada
(c) Indus
(d) Kaveri

Column II:
(i) Arabian Sea
(ii) Bay of Bengal
(iii) Arabian Sea (via Pakistan)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Ganga drains into Bay of Bengal (ii). Narmada into Arabian Sea (i). Indus into Arabian Sea via Pakistan (iii). Kaveri into Bay of Bengal (ii). Option 2 swaps Ganga and Narmada. Option 3 swaps Narmada and Indus. Option 4 swaps Ganga and Indus.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Sambhar Lake in Rajasthan is significant because:
options: It is India's largest freshwater lake
It is India's largest inland salt water lake and a major source of salt production
It is located at the highest altitude in India
questions.correctAnswer: It is India's largest inland salt water lake and a major source of salt production
questions.explanation: Sambhar Lake is India's largest inland saline/salt lake, used for salt production since ancient times. India's largest freshwater lake is Wular (J&K). It is natural, not man-made. It is in the plains of Rajasthan, not at high altitude.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Krishna river:

(i) It originates near Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra.
(ii) It flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.
(iii) Tungabhadra, Bhima, and Musi are its major tributaries.
(iv) It drains into the Arabian Sea.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Krishna rises near Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats. (ii) is correct — flows through 4 states. (iii) is correct — all are major tributaries. (iv) is wrong — Krishna flows EAST and drains into the Bay of Bengal near Vijayawada, NOT the Arabian Sea.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Ganga-Brahmaputra Delta (Sundarbans) is the largest river delta in the world.
Reason (R): Both the Ganga and Brahmaputra carry enormous quantities of sediment that are deposited at their combined mouth, building up the vast deltaic region.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — the Sundarbans delta (~105,000 km²) is the world's largest. (R) is correct — massive sediment loads from both rivers create and expand the delta. (R) explains (A) because the enormous combined sediment deposition is the direct cause of the delta's record-breaking size.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are man-made lakes/reservoirs in India?

(i) Gobind Sagar (on Sutlej, Himachal Pradesh)
(ii) Nagarjuna Sagar (on Krishna, Telangana)
(iii) Dal Lake (Srinagar, J&K)
(iv) Hirakud Reservoir (on Mahanadi, Odisha)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Gobind Sagar (i) is the reservoir behind Bhakra Dam. Nagarjuna Sagar (ii) is a dam reservoir. Hirakud (iv) is the world's longest earthen dam reservoir. Dal Lake (iii) is a NATURAL lake in Srinagar, not man-made.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following lakes with their states:

Column I:
(a) Vembanad Lake
(b) Loktak Lake
(c) Pangong Tso
(d) Pulicat Lake

Column II:
(i) Manipur
(ii) Kerala
(iii) Ladakh
(iv) Andhra Pradesh/Tamil Nadu border

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Vembanad is in Kerala (ii) — longest lake in India. Loktak is in Manipur (i) — famous for floating islands (phumdis). Pangong Tso is in Ladakh (iii) — high-altitude lake on India-China border. Pulicat is on the Andhra Pradesh/Tamil Nadu border (iv) — a brackish lagoon.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Indus river enters India through which state/UT?
questions.explanation: The Indus enters India from Tibet into Ladakh UT near Demchok in the southeast. It then flows northwest through Ladakh (Leh) before entering Pakistan. Himachal Pradesh has Sutlej and Beas. Punjab is downstream. J&K (UT) has Jhelum and Chenab but not where Indus enters India.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Yamuna river:

(i) It originates from Yamunotri glacier in Uttarakhand.
(ii) It is the longest tributary of the Ganga.
(iii) Delhi is situated on the banks of the Yamuna.
(iv) The Yamuna flows independently into the Bay of Bengal.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Yamuna rises from Yamunotri glacier. (ii) is correct — at 1,376 km, it's the Ganga's longest tributary. (iii) is correct — Delhi is on the Yamuna's banks. (iv) is wrong — the Yamuna does NOT flow independently to the sea; it MERGES with the Ganga at Prayagraj (Allahabad) and then the Ganga continues to the Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna, and the mythological Saraswati at Prayagraj (Allahabad) is called __________.
questions.explanation: Triveni Sangam ('triple confluence') is where Ganga, Yamuna, and the invisible Saraswati meet at Prayagraj — a major Hindu pilgrimage site. 'Sangam' alone means any confluence. Devprayag is where Bhagirathi and Alaknanda meet to form the Ganga. Gangotri is the Ganga's glacier source.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Himalayan rivers are perennial (flow year-round), while most peninsular rivers are seasonal.
Reason (R): Himalayan rivers are fed by glacial melt in addition to rainfall, ensuring continuous flow; peninsular rivers mostly depend solely on monsoon rainfall.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — Himalayan rivers (Ganga, Brahmaputra) flow year-round while many peninsular rivers reduce significantly in summer. (R) is correct — glacial melt provides water even during dry seasons. (R) explains (A) because the dual source (glacier + rain) is what makes Himalayan rivers perennial while rain-only peninsular rivers are seasonal.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following rivers form the boundary between two states?

(i) Narmada — between MP and Maharashtra (partially)
(ii) Godavari — between Maharashtra and Telangana (partially)
(iii) Kaveri — source of interstate dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu
(iv) Ganga — between Bihar and Jharkhand (partially)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: All four correctly identify rivers that form or relate to interstate boundaries/disputes. Narmada (i) forms part of the MP-Maharashtra border. Godavari (ii) borders Maharashtra-Telangana in sections. Kaveri (iii) is a famous water-sharing dispute. Ganga (iv) separates Bihar and Jharkhand at points.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following rivers with their approximate lengths in India:

Column I:
(a) Ganga
(b) Godavari
(c) Krishna
(d) Narmada

Column II:
(i) ~1,312 km
(ii) ~2,525 km
(iii) ~1,465 km
(iv) ~1,400 km

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Ganga ≈ 2,525 km (ii). Godavari ≈ 1,465 km (iii). Krishna ≈ 1,400 km (iv). Narmada ≈ 1,312 km (i). Option 2 swaps Ganga and Godavari. Option 3 swaps Godavari and Krishna. Option 4 swaps Ganga and Narmada.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Loktak Lake in Manipur is unique because:
options: It is the saltiest lake in India
It has floating islands called 'phumdis' and the Keibul Lamjao National Park floats on it
It is the deepest lake in India
It is located at sea level
questions.correctAnswer: It has floating islands called 'phumdis' and the Keibul Lamjao National Park floats on it
questions.explanation: Loktak is famous for phumdis (floating heterogeneous masses of vegetation) and hosts the world's only floating national park (Keibul Lamjao), home to the endangered Sangai deer. It's freshwater, not salty. It's not the deepest. It's at elevation (~768 m), not sea level.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Mahanadi river:

(i) It originates in Chhattisgarh and flows through Odisha.
(ii) The Hirakud Dam, one of the world's longest dams, is built on it.
(iii) It drains into the Bay of Bengal.
(iv) It is a west-flowing river draining into the Arabian Sea.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Mahanadi rises near Sihawa in Chhattisgarh. (ii) is correct — Hirakud Dam (25.8 km) is on the Mahanadi in Odisha. (iii) is correct — it drains into the Bay of Bengal forming a delta. (iv) is wrong — Mahanadi flows EAST, not west.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Inter-state river water disputes are common in India, such as the Kaveri, Krishna, and Narmada water disputes.
Reason (R): Multiple states share the waters of these rivers, and growing populations and agricultural demands create competition for limited water resources.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — Karnataka-TN (Kaveri), Maharashtra-Karnataka-AP-Telangana (Krishna), and MP-Gujarat-Maharashtra (Narmada) disputes are well-known. (R) is correct — multiple states sharing rivers + increasing demand = conflict. (R) explains (A) by identifying the underlying cause of these disputes.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The Vembanad Lake in Kerala is notable for which of the following reasons?

(i) It is the longest lake in India.
(ii) The famous Nehru Trophy Boat Race is held here.
(iii) Willingdon Island (Kochi port) is located in this lake.
(iv) It is a freshwater lake with no connection to the sea.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — at ~96 km, Vembanad is India's longest lake. (ii) is correct — the snake boat race is a major event. (iii) is correct — Willingdon Island was created from dredging Vembanad. (iv) is wrong — Vembanad is a BRACKISH lagoon connected to the Arabian Sea; it's not purely freshwater.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following dams with the rivers they are built on:

Column I:
(a) Bhakra Nangal Dam
(b) Tehri Dam
(c) Sardar Sarovar Dam
(d) Nagarjuna Sagar Dam

Column II:
(i) Narmada
(ii) Sutlej
(iii) Bhagirathi
(iv) Krishna

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Bhakra Nangal is on the Sutlej (ii). Tehri Dam is on the Bhagirathi (iii). Sardar Sarovar is on the Narmada (i). Nagarjuna Sagar is on the Krishna (iv). Option 2 swaps Bhakra and Tehri. Option 3 swaps Tehri and Sardar Sarovar. Option 4 swaps Bhakra and Nagarjuna.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indus river system:

(i) The Indus originates near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet.
(ii) Its major Indian tributaries are Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej.
(iii) Under the Indus Waters Treaty, India has full rights over the Indus, Jhelum, and Chenab.
(iv) The Indus is one of the longest rivers in Asia.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Indus rises from Bokhar Chu glacier near Mansarovar. (ii) is correct — these five rivers (Panjnad) form the Indus system in India/Pakistan. (iv) is correct — at ~3,180 km, it's one of Asia's longest rivers. (iii) is wrong — under the Indus Waters Treaty, India has full rights over EASTERN rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej), NOT the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab which are allocated to Pakistan).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Narmada does not form a delta at its mouth.
Reason (R): The Narmada flows through a rift valley with hard rocky bed, carrying less sediment, and its narrow mouth with strong tidal action prevents delta formation.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — the Narmada forms an estuary (not a delta) at the Gulf of Khambhat. (R) is correct — less sediment (due to hard rift valley floor) + narrow channel + tidal action prevents delta building. (R) explains (A) by describing the geological and hydrological reasons for the absence of a delta.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ river is the second longest peninsular river after the Godavari.
questions.explanation: Krishna (~1,400 km) is the second longest peninsular river after Godavari (~1,465 km). Narmada (~1,312 km) is third. Mahanadi (~858 km) and Kaveri (~800 km) are shorter.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following lakes are designated as Ramsar Wetland Sites in India?

(i) Chilika Lake (Odisha)
(ii) Wular Lake (J&K)
(iii) Loktak Lake (Manipur)
(iv) Sambhar Lake (Rajasthan)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: All four are Ramsar sites: Chilika (designated 1981), Wular (1990), Loktak (1990), and Sambhar (1990). India has over 75 Ramsar sites as of recent years, and all major lakes listed here have been recognized for their ecological importance.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Kaveri (Cauvery) river:

(i) It originates at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Karnataka.
(ii) It flows through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
(iii) The famous Shivasamudram Falls and Hogenakkal Falls are on the Kaveri.
(iv) It is the longest river in India.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Kaveri rises at Talakaveri, Coorg (Kodagu), Karnataka. (ii) is correct — flows through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu (and touches Kerala/Puducherry briefly). (iii) is correct — both waterfalls are on the Kaveri. (iv) is wrong — Kaveri (~800 km) is NOT the longest; Ganga (~2,525 km) is the longest in India.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following lakes with their types:

Column I:
(a) Chilika Lake
(b) Wular Lake
(c) Sambhar Lake
(d) Gobind Sagar

Column II:
(i) Freshwater (natural)
(ii) Brackish water (lagoon)
(iii) Saline/Salt lake
(iv) Man-made reservoir

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Chilika is a brackish water lagoon (ii). Wular is a natural freshwater lake (i). Sambhar is a saline/salt lake (iii). Gobind Sagar is a man-made reservoir behind Bhakra Dam (iv). Option 2 swaps Chilika and Wular types. Option 3 swaps Wular and Sambhar. Option 4 swaps Chilika and Gobind Sagar.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Brahmaputra is called by different names in different regions: Tsangpo in Tibet, Dihang/Siang in Arunachal Pradesh, and Brahmaputra in Assam.
Reason (R): Major rivers often receive local names as they pass through different regions, reflecting the languages and cultures of those areas.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — Brahmaputra has different names in different regions. (R) is correct — local naming reflects regional languages (Tibetan, tribal languages, Assamese). (R) explains (A) because the practice of renaming rivers locally is the direct reason for the multiple names.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Son river is a major tributary of which river?
questions.explanation: The Son river is a major RIGHT-bank tributary of the Ganga, originating in Amarkantak (MP) and joining the Ganga near Patna in Bihar. It is not a tributary of Yamuna, Godavari, or Narmada.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the importance of rivers in India:

(i) Rivers provide water for irrigation, supporting agriculture.
(ii) Hydroelectric power is generated from river dams.
(iii) Rivers facilitate inland water transport.
(iv) Rivers have no cultural or religious significance in India.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — canals from rivers irrigate vast farmlands. (ii) is correct — dams like Bhakra, Tehri generate hydroelectricity. (iii) is correct — National Waterways on Ganga, Brahmaputra etc. support transport. (iv) is wrong — rivers are deeply sacred in Indian culture (Ganga, Yamuna, Kaveri are worshipped).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to frequent flooding?
questions.explanation: The Kosi river is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because it frequently changes course and causes devastating floods in Bihar. The Ganga also floods but is not called this. Son and Gandak don't carry this title.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the drainage area of major Indian river basins:

| River | Drainage Area (lakh km²) |
|-------|---------------------------|
| Ganga | 8.6 |
| Indus (Indian part) | 3.2 |
| Godavari | 3.1 |
| Krishna | 2.6 |
| Brahmaputra (Indian part) | 1.9 |

Which river basin covers the largest area in India?
questions.explanation: The Ganga basin at 8.6 lakh km² is the largest river basin in India, covering about 26% of India's area. Indus (Indian portion) is 3.2 lakh km². Godavari is 3.1 lakh km². Brahmaputra (Indian) is 1.9 lakh km².

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the number of states through which major rivers flow:

| River | States |
|-------|--------|
| Ganga | 5 |
| Godavari | 7 |
| Krishna | 4 |
| Narmada | 3 |
| Brahmaputra | 3 |

Which river passes through the maximum number of states?
questions.explanation: Godavari flows through 7 states (Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Karnataka) — the most of any Indian river shown. Ganga passes through 5. Krishna through 4. Narmada through 3.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following National Waterways is on the Ganga river?
questions.explanation: National Waterway 1 is on the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system from Prayagraj (Allahabad) to Haldia. NW-2 is on Brahmaputra. NW-3 is on Kerala backwaters. NW-4 is on Krishna-Godavari-Buckingham Canal system.
